judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional list of what the Contract Documents consist of, closing with an exclusion of bidding requirements 'except as specifically enumerated in the Agreement'. Clear in structure; 'other documents listed in the Agreement' is the only open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 15, whose Specifications, Drawings and Project Manual entries are blank or 'TBD', and against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4/3.10.5, which make later-developed schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents without enumeration. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause plus 'The Contract may be amended or modified only by Modification' and a four-part no-privity list. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5, under which schedules and cost estimates become Contract Documents automatically 'as they are developed' rather than by Modification, and against Agreement Article 1's own integration clause. Genuine inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of 'Work' covering construction and services 'required by the Contract Documents ... whether completed or partially completed'. Standard and bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 2 and First Addendum Article 2 [Revised]; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Project as the total construction of which the Work may be the whole or a part. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 6.1.1 (Owner's right to perform separate construction) and the Agreement's Project identification; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Drawings as the graphic portions of the Contract Documents. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 15.1.5, where the list of Drawings is left blank or 'TBD', and Supplementary Conditions 3.10.5, under which drawings arrive in phases; the definition has no identified referent. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Specifications as the written requirements for materials, systems, standards and workmanship. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 15.1.4, whose Specifications table is blank and whose Project Manual date is missing; the defined term has nothing to attach to. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Project Manual is a volume assembled for the Work which may include the bidding requirements, sample forms, Conditions of the Contract and Specifications' — 'may include' makes the contents of a defined document optional and unfixed. Modest but nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 15.1.3/15.1.4, which refer to 'the Project Manual dated ___' with the date left blank and the document list 'TBD'; the incorporation chain fails. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Performance is required 'only to the extent consistent with the Contract Documents and reasonably inferable from them as being necessary to produce the indicated results' — 'reasonably inferable' is the classic contested scope standard in construction contracts. Nameable and genuinely two-sided.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.2.6 (further development 'reasonably inferable therefrom' but excluding scope changes) and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1 (better quality/greater quantity); three overlapping scope rules with different tests. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says the organisation of the Specifications and arrangement of Drawings shall not control the division of Work among Subcontractors. Definite and narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 10.1 and A201 5.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Words with 'well-known technical or construction industry meanings' are used accordingly — the rule itself imports an external, unfixed vocabulary and 'well-known' is undefined. A modest interpretive hook.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 1.4.1 and Agreement Article 1; the interpretive rules are consistent with one another. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A capitalisation convention identifying three categories of capitalised terms. Mechanical and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 1.1's defined terms; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An express instruction that the omission of modifiers such as 'all' and 'any' and articles 'is not intended to affect the interpretation of either statement'. A clause telling courts to disregard textual differences is itself an interpretive instrument that can be pressed either way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 1.2.3 and Agreement Article 1; the interpretive rules cohere. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contract Documents to be signed and, if not all signed, for the Architect to identify unsigned documents on request. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the First Addendum and Supplementary Conditions execution blocks, which are undated ('this __ day of ___, 2002') and in part unsigned in this instrument; the clause anticipates but does not resolve that. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Execution operates as a representation that the Contractor visited the site and correlated observations. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 14.6(d), which contains the same representation, and A201 3.2.1; duplication rather than conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, carefully drafted copyright and instruments-of-service clause with explicit permissions and a record-set carve-out. Length is not ambiguity; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.1.5/1.1.6 and 3.11.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly mangled here, but the operative content — the Owner furnishing a correct statement of record legal title within fifteen days of a written request — is a definite obligation. The garbling is the main source of uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 4.1 (Owner's time to file mortgages and mechanic's liens, left blank) and A201 8.2.2; the blank leaves a related timing question unanswered but no direct conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made to fulfill the Owner's obligations' is an open standard, and making it 'a condition precedent to commencement or continuation of the Work' gives the Contractor a powerful, ill-defined stop-work lever. Both 'reasonable evidence' and 'materially vary' are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 14.1.1.4 (Contractor may terminate if the Owner fails to furnish such evidence) and Agreement 5.1.1/5.2.1, where no Contract Sum or GMP is stated; what the Owner must show is unusually hard to determine here. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates easements, assessments and charges to the Owner except permits and fees under 3.7.1. A clean division with a stated exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.7.1 and Agreement 7.6.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Owner furnishes surveys and a legal description; the Contractor 'shall be entitled to rely on the accuracy of information furnished by the Owner but shall exercise proper precautions'. The reliance/precaution pairing is a mild tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.2.1 (Contractor to take field measurements and study the documents) and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(b) ('no extra charge ... on account of differences between actual dimensions and the dimensions indicated'); reliance and the no-extra-charge rule pull against each other. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and 'any other information or services relevant to the Contractor's performance ... under the Owner's control' — both soft, though conventional. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.2.11 (Architect's interpretations) and 8.3.1 (delay caused by the Owner); the duty is enforceable through the claims machinery. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Copies 'as are reasonably necessary for execution of the Work' furnished free of charge. Narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.5.4 (document reproduction costs reimbursed) and A201 1.6.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A right to stop the Work where the Contractor 'persistently fails to carry out Work in accordance with the Contract Documents', coupled with an express disclaimer of any duty to exercise it. 'Persistently' is soft but the disclaimer is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 2.4.1 and Supplementary Conditions 2.4.1, and A201 14.2.1; the remedies are cumulative. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully staged two-notice cure procedure with a defined seven-day period at each stage, plus Change Order deduction and Architect approval. Internally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 2.4.1, which revises this to a single seven-day notice and omits the second notice entirely, while the Supplementary Conditions preamble says 'the unaltered provision of the General Conditions shall remain in effect'; whether one or two notices are required is genuinely open. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition identifying the Contractor and its authorised representative. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 14.4 (representative named with a built-in succession) and 14.5; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contractor shall perform the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents.' Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 2 and First Addendum Article 2 [Revised]; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor is not relieved by the Architect's administration or by tests and approvals by others. A clear non-waiver rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.2.3 and 3.12.8; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause both says the study obligations are 'not for the purpose of discovering errors, omissions, or inconsistencies' and requires any such errors discovered to be reported promptly. That internal push-pull, plus 'carefully study and compare', is a familiar construction battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(b) (verify measurements and bear responsibility, no extra compensation) and A201 3.2.3; the Supplementary Condition shifts risk further onto the Contractor than 3.2.1 contemplates. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires prompt reporting of noted design errors while disclaiming any duty to review as a licensed design professional. The gap between 'noted' and 'should have noted' is the arguable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.3, 3.12.10 and Supplementary Conditions 3.12.7.1; the disclaimers are consistent across those provisions. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A liability allocation whose final sentence turns on whether the Contractor 'recognized such error, inconsistency, omission or difference and knowingly failed to report it' — a knowledge-and-intent test embedded in a cost-allocation rule. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.3.6 and 4.3.7 (claims routes) and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(b), which bars extra compensation for dimensional differences outright. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The warranty text as it appears is fragmentary, and its exclusions — 'improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage' — are open-ended evaluative categories that swallow a good deal of the warranty. Both the truncation and the exclusions are nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 12.2.2 (one-year correction period), 9.10.4.3 (special warranties survive final payment) and Supplementary Conditions 9.10.1.1; the warranty scheme is spread across several provisions with different time limits. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor 'shall pay sales, consumer, use and similar taxes ... which are legally enacted when bids are received or negotiations concluded, whether or not yet effective'. The timing test is precise; 'similar' is the only soft word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.6.2 (such taxes reimbursed as a Cost of the Work) and Exhibit D (Hawaii General Excise Tax 'included as a job cost'); on a cost-plus contract 'the Contractor shall pay' and 'the Owner reimburses' point in different directions. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Allocates the building permit and other permits to the Contractor 'unless otherwise provided in the Contract Documents', limited to those 'customarily secured after execution' and 'legally required when bids are received or negotiations concluded'. Layered qualifiers but each is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.6.3 (permit fees reimbursed as a Cost of the Work), A201 2.2.2 and First Addendum 4.1 ('pending approval of permits'); who bears the cost and the delay risk of permits is addressed in three places. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A general compliance obligation with laws and lawful orders. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.3 and 3.7.4; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says it is not the Contractor's responsibility to ascertain that the Contract Documents comply with law, but requires notice if the Contractor 'observes' a variance. The observe/should-have-observed line is the arguable point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.4, which imposes cost responsibility if the Contractor performs Work 'knowing it to be contrary' to law, and 3.2.2; the two use different mental-state triggers but harmonise. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cost responsibility attaches where the Contractor performs Work 'knowing it to be contrary' to law without notice. A clear knowledge standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.7.3 and 8.1.6 of the Agreement; consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contractor to include 'all allowances stated in the Contract Documents' and to accept Owner direction on suppliers, subject to reasonable objection. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.2.4, where the allowances entry is blank; the whole allowance mechanism has no content in this contract. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Divides allowance content between materials 'delivered at the site' and the Contractor's unloading, handling, overhead and profit, with Change Order adjustment for the difference. Detailed but arithmetically clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.2.4 (blank) and 6.1/6.4; with no allowances stated the adjustment machinery is idle. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Owner must select allowance materials 'in sufficient time to avoid delay' — an open timing standard, though the purpose is obvious. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 5.2.4 (blank) and A201 8.3.1; without stated allowances there is nothing to select. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires 'a competent superintendent and necessary assistants who shall be in attendance at the Project site during performance of the Work'. 'Competent' and 'in attendance' are evaluative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum Article 2 [Revised], which requires one designated supervisory employee who 'personally shall supervise and attend to the Work' and may take other work only if it does not impair this Work; the two staffing requirements overlap without being aligned. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires a submittal schedule kept current for the Architect's approval, coordinated with the construction schedule. Clear duty, garbled text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4/3.10.5 and 1.1.2.1 (Owner's concurrence also required); cumulative. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Contractor shall perform the Work in general accordance with the most recent schedules submitted to the Owner and Architect' — 'general accordance' is a deliberately loose standard for a schedule obligation. Nameable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4, which requires monitoring 'for conformance with the requirements of the Construction Schedule' and makes the schedule a Contract Document; 'general accordance' and 'conformance' are different standards for the same duty. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A record-keeping duty for one marked-up set of documents delivered at completion. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.6.1 (record set retained by the Contractor) and 9.10.2; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Shop Drawings. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.4 and Supplementary Conditions 3.12.7.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Product Data. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.4-3.12.5; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of Samples as physical examples establishing standards by which the Work will be judged. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.4 and 4.2.7; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States that submittals 'are not Contract Documents' and explains their limited purpose. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5, which do make later-developed schedules and cost estimates part of the Contract Documents; the categorical statement here and the self-incorporating supplements sit uneasily. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires review, approval and submission 'with reasonable promptness and in such sequence as to cause no delay'. Ordinary softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.2.7 and Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A representation of what approving and submitting a submittal means. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.8 and 4.2.7; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deviations are excused only if the Contractor 'specifically informed the Architect in writing of such deviation at the time of submittal' and the Architect gave written approval 'to the specific deviation as a minor change'. Layered conditions, but each is expressed precisely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 4.2.7 (limited purpose of Architect's review), 7.4.1 (minor changes) and Supplementary Conditions 1.2.1.1(c); consistent. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires written attention to revisions on resubmittals, with a consequence if omitted. Clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.12.8 and 4.2.7; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long allocation of design-professional responsibility turning on whether services 'constitute the practice of architecture or engineering' and whether the Owner and Architect 'specified all performance and design criteria'. Those conditions are genuinely contestable, though drafted with care.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 3.12.7.1 (shop drawings by a licensed engineer 'if required by the Architect or the Owner or applicable law') and 3.2.2; the supplements add a requirement without adjusting the criteria condition here. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site with materials or equipment' — 'unreasonably encumber' is an open standard, but a narrow one. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.2.1 (opportunity for separate contractors) and 3.15; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Responsibility for cutting, fitting and patching 'required to complete the Work or to make its parts fit together properly'. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.2.5, which extends the same responsibilities to separate contractors; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prohibits damaging or altering others' construction except with written consent 'not to be unreasonably withheld', with a reciprocal duty on the Contractor. Balanced and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 6.2.4 and 10.2.1.3; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An access provision, truncated in this text, requiring access to the Work in preparation and progress wherever located. Little content to construe beyond the truncation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement Article 11 (accounting records access) and A201 13.5; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor pays royalties and defends infringement suits 'but shall not be responsible for such defense or loss when a particular design, process or product of a particular manufacturer or manufacturers is required by the Contract Documents' — unless the Contractor 'has reason to believe' there is infringement and fails to report it. The 'reason to believe' trigger is the soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Agreement 7.6.5, which reimburses royalties, defence costs and settlements as a Cost of the Work but excludes them from the Fee and 'the Guaranteed Maximum Price'; that clause allocates the same risk to the Owner on a cost basis while this one leaves it with the Contractor. Real tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An indemnity 'to the fullest extent permitted by law' and 'to the extent claims ... are not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance', limited to injury and property damage 'but only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions' of the Contractor's chain, 'regardless of whether or not such claim ... is caused in part by a party indemnified hereunder'. The 'to the fullest extent permitted by law' opener and the interaction of the proportionality limit with the caused-in-part clause are classic construction points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 11.3.1 (Project Management Protective Liability insurance is optional and was not required here) and 11.1.1.8, and against Agreement Article 16, which is blank; the insurance-based carve-out has no referent. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard anti-immunity clause preserving the indemnity notwithstanding workers' compensation limits. Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 3.18.1 and 11.1.1.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition of the Architect and its authorised representative. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Agreement's identification of the Architect and 4.1.3 (successor Architect); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Architect's duties 'shall not be restricted, modified or extended without written consent of the Owner, Contractor and Architect', consent 'not to be unreasonably withheld'. Clear as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Supplementary Conditions 1.1.2.1, which requires the Owner's express written consent wherever the Architect's is required and reserves control 'for purposes of aesthetic and cost control of the Work'; that is a material modification of the Architect's role effected by a document the Contractor signed, but its fit with the tri-party consent requirement is arguable. Real tension.
